paper.title_en: Rapid prediction and multi-objective optimization of mechanical response of the CEPC detector barrel yoke based on data-driven surrogate models
paper.abstract_en: The iterative design optimization of the Circular Electron Positron Collider (CEPC) detector barrel yoke relies on time-consuming finite element analysis (FEA), leading to low computational efficiency. This paper proposes a rapid prediction and multi-objective optimization method based on data-driven surrogate models. Using 1500 FEA samples generated by latin hypercube sampling, three algorithms—support vector regression (SVR), extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), and multilayer perceptron (MLP)—are employed to predict the maximum deformation and maximum equivalent stress of the barrel yoke, and first-order and second-order polynomial response surfaces are introduced as traditional baselines. Among the three machine learning models, SVR achieves the best overall performance, with test set <math altimg="si3.svg" display="inline" id="d1e1624"><msup><mrow><mi>R</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math> values of 0.9998 and 0.9651. The second-order response surface reaches comparable accuracy, indicating that for the low-dimensional optimization problem of the barrel yoke, polynomial surrogates are likewise effective. Using SVR, the NSGA-II algorithm performs multi-objective optimization of the end flange mass and the barrel yoke maximum deformation, yielding 100 Pareto optimal solutions. The knee point lies at a mass of 41.8 t and a deformation of 1.55 mm, before which an additional 5.7 t of mass yields a 22.5% deformation reduction, after which the marginal cost rises sharply. The entire workflow completes in approximately 6 s, about six orders of magnitude faster than conventional FEA, validating the “parametric modeling–surrogate modeling–multi-objective optimization” pipeline and offering a reference for rapid design optimization of other subdetector structures. •SVR models achieve R<sup loc="post">2</sup> = 0.9998 and 0.9651 for barrel yoke max deformation and max equivalent stress.•NSGA-II yields 100 Pareto solutions for end flange mass-deformation optimization.•Knee point at 41.8 t, 1.55 mm marks the critical mass-stiffness trade-off region.•Optimization completes in 6 s: a speedup of six orders of magnitude over conventional FEA.•Parametric-surrogate-optimization workflow validated for CEPC detector structural design.
